name: DNS Challenge: Deep Noise Suppression Challenge Benchmark
description: The INTERSPEECH 2020 Deep Noise Suppression (DNS) Challenge dataset (Challenge 1) is an audio benchmark designed to train and evaluate neural models on real-time single-channel speech enhancement. It provides 500 hours of clean speech from 2,150 speakers (derived from LibriVox, with approx. 441 usable hours), 180 hours of environmental noise across 150 classes (from AudioSet, Freesound, and DEMAND), and measured/synthetic room impulse responses.

license.name: Mixed License (CC-BY-4.0 Repository / Mixed Source Audio Terms)
license.notes: Microsoft distributes repository scripts and synthesis code under MIT, and the dataset repository under CC-BY-4.0. Underlying audio sources retain original terms: clean speech is derived from public domain LibriVox audiobooks; noise clips include YouTube audio from Google AudioSet and community audio from Freesound/DEMAND (carrying varied attribution and non-commercial terms); synthetic/measured RIRs are from Microsoft. Unrestricted commercial exploitation of all components is not cleared.

verification.notes: Verified against Interspeech 2020 publication (DOI: 10.21437/Interspeech.2020-3038, ISCA Archive) and official Microsoft repository. Clean speech from LibriVox (500h total, ~441h usable, 2150 speakers), noise from AudioSet/Freesound/DEMAND (~70,000 clips, 150 classes, 180h), and 3,000 room impulse responses.

size.notes: 16kHz 16-bit uncompressed WAV files of speech, environmental noise, and impulse responses across wideband challenge tracks.
